blocks.x: Voice and chat agents that resolve more without losing trust: grounded answers, dignified handoffs that carry full context, streaming voice inside real-time budgets, and nightly dialog evaluation that measures containment honestly.
Containment and trust are one metric, not two

Conversational systems are judged on containment and trust at the same time: resolve more without human help, and never strand a customer mid-issue. The build is dialogue design, retrieval grounding, handoff choreography and voice engineering — with the metrics wired before the first transcript.

Digital humans add a presentation layer, not a magic one. The avatar succeeds when the conversation underneath is grounded, the handoffs are dignified, and the voice stack holds latency budgets on real networks.
What follows is the build anatomy: the failure modes that inflate containment while destroying CSAT, the architecture that holds both, and the console that keeps the trade visible every day.
Four failure modes that inflate containment and destroy trust
Each of these produces a dashboard that looks great in the monthly review and a customer base that quietly stops using the channel — the countermeasures target the trust side of the ledger.

widgets.title: Voice turn budget — each hop against its cap
widgets.note: Gauges show each hop against its cap with warn/crit bands. Total budget 1.2 s at p95 — the endpointing gauge is the one to watch; it eats whatever the others leave behind.

widgets.title: The conversation stack — click nodes for their contract

nodes.label: Audio capture
nodes.detail: Streaming capture with VAD and jitter buffer; packet loss concealment keeps ASR fed through network hiccups.

nodes.label: Streaming ASR
nodes.detail: Partial hypotheses from 120 ms chunks drive prefetch; finalization triggers the reasoning turn with confidence stamped.

nodes.label: Endpointing policy
nodes.detail: Adaptive endpointer tuned per locale and call type; barge-in cancels generation mid-token and rewinds dialogue state.

nodes.label: Intent & signals
nodes.detail: Classifies distress, legal exposure, VIP status — signals route the turn before generation, not after.

nodes.label: Grounded generation
nodes.detail: Retrieval-grounded with citations attached to claims; the persona prompt and policy gate are versioned artifacts.

nodes.label: Policy gate
nodes.detail: Screens against commitment rules per channel; blocked responses regenerate with a safer strategy and log the block.

nodes.label: Streaming synthesis
nodes.detail: Sentence-chunked synthesis; prosody profile is part of the persona contract and A/B tested like copy.

nodes.label: Escalation bridge
nodes.detail: Warm handoff with transcript, evidence and predicted intent — the human agent never asks the customer to repeat.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read each contract. The escalation bridge is a first-class lane: handoffs carry full context by design.

blocks.caption: Conversational AI & Digital Humans: default stack and the conditions under which we deviate
rows: NLU & state
LLM-based state tracking with typed slots
Classic NLU only for tiny, closed intent sets with hard latency floors
Grounding
Same RAG spine as knowledge domain, scoped per channel
Un-grounded generation on policy topics — permanently barred
Voice
Streaming ASR → LLM → neural TTS with barge-in
Cascaded non-streaming stack — it fails the latency budget on cellular
Guardrails
Topic, PII and advisability guards per jurisdiction
Global one-size guard config — jurisdictions differ and audits notice
Handoff
Skill-based routing with context packs
Blind transfer to generic queues — it wastes the automation's work
Analytics
Transcript-level eval with intent-family scorecards
Only aggregate CSAT — it hides exactly the intents that need work
